Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovTech Solutions Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to InnovTech Solutions’ Third Quarter Earnings Call. Joining me today are Michael Carter, CEO; Susan Lee, CFO; David Chen, COO; and Emily Rodriguez, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Michael Carter.

Michael Carter, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, let's dissect the Q3 performance and Q4 outlook for net margin and diluted EPS. We delivered a strong Q3, with diluted EPS coming in at $0.41, significantly exceeding our initial guidance of $0.20. This $0.21 beat, representing a remarkable 105% positive surprise against our internal forecasts, is primarily attributable to a combination of robust revenue growth, improved operational efficiency, and favorable currency tailwinds. We anticipate continued momentum as we move into Q4, projecting a diluted EPS of $0.44. This reflects our confidence in the continued strength of our core business.

We also continued to drive improvements through our foundry partnerships, especially with GlobalFoundries. This quarter marks a significant milestone: we received our first foundry prepay under the restructured LTA with GlobalFoundries, our primary silicon foundry partner. This prepay, amounting to $175 million, is tied to specific wafer commitments over the next two years, primarily for our high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) product lines. This will enable more efficient production and cost management, which further bolsters our overall financial health.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our State of Ohio capital grant, where we’ve received a capital grant of $75 million from the State of Ohio in Q3. This grant is specifically earmarked for the expansion of our advanced manufacturing facility in Delaware County, Ohio. The facility focuses on the production of next-generation microchips crucial for the automotive and aerospace industries.

Now I’ll hand it over to Susan Lee to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Susan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Michael, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our Q3 revenue reached a robust $14.2 billion, representing a 9% sequential increase from Q2's $13.03 billion and a substantial outperformance against the midpoint of our Q3 guidance, which stood at $13.45 billion. This $750 million beat reflects strong execution across all major lines of business and a favorable macroeconomic environment in select key regions has contributed meaningfully to our overall performance. We are projecting revenue in the range of $14.6 billion to $15.6 billion for Q4 2023.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our enhanced inventory management strategy, with a net inventory reduction of $500 million this quarter, translating to a significant decrease of 7 days in DOI. Our DOI now stands at 68 days, compared to 75 days in Q2 2024 and 77 days in Q3 2023, which translates to reduced holding costs, decreased risk of obsolescence, and improved working capital efficiency.

And although still early, our continued engagement with government agencies to secure financial incentives is proving fruitful. As part of the incentives packages, we have secured low-interest loans from both the State of Ohio and potential European partners. The Ohio loan, at a rate of 2.5%, totals $25 million and is intended to cover a portion of the infrastructure upgrades needed for the Delaware County facility expansion.

With that, I’ll turn it to David Chen for a deeper look at operational performance.

David Chen, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was our net margin expansion, which reached 12.5% in Q3, a 250 basis point improvement compared to 10.0% in Q3 of the previous year, particularly in North America and Asia-Pacific, where we saw the strongest revenue growth.

Additionally, our improved inventory management has enabled more efficient production schedules and faster inventory turnover. One example is the implementation of "Kanban" systems at our primary manufacturing facility in Ohio, resulting in a 15% reduction in work-in-progress inventory.

We’re also seeing early traction in our foundry business, where updated processes and technological advancements are attracting significant customer interest. The headline here is the significant commitment we've secured from a major customer. While confidentiality agreements prevent me from naming the client directly, I can state that this is a North American-based fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-performance computing (HPC) and AI accelerators. This customer has officially committed to utilizing both our Intel 18A and Intel 3 process technologies for their next-generation product lines. The commitment encompasses multiple product tape-outs over the next three years, with initial production slated for late 2026 on Intel 18A and mid-2027 on Intel 3.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily Rodriguez for the tech and product update.

Emily Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our foundry partnerships, supporting broader adoption and helping to secure commitments from two additional customers for our Intel 18A process. These are earlier-stage engagements, focused on design exploration and test chip fabrication. One is a European-based company specializing in automotive semiconductors focused on advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). They are evaluating Intel 18A for its potential to deliver the performance required for Level 4 and Level 5 autonomous driving applications while meeting stringent automotive reliability requirements. Initial test chip design and fabrication are expected to commence in Q1 2025.

We’ve also supported our CapEx investment in renewable energy sources, particularly solar and wind power purchase agreements (PPAs) and on-site generation at our North American facilities, and are increasingly qualifying for attractive government incentives under the Inflation Reduction Act.

And finally, on our government grant initiatives, our new architecture will allow us to continue to work closely with the U.S. CHIPS Office on the review of our four U.S. applications for federal funding.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the State of Ohio capital grant and whether you foresee similar opportunities in other states?

Michael Carter:
Yes, absolutely. The Ohio grant is part of a broader strategy to leverage state and federal incentives to support our manufacturing expansion. We are actively exploring similar opportunities in other states, particularly those with a strong focus on semiconductor manufacturing and workforce development. We believe that these incentives are crucial for maintaining our competitiveness in the global market and ensuring a stable and skilled workforce.

Analyst 2:
On the Q3 revenue beat, how much was driven by the strategic pricing adjustments versus increased volume?

Susan Lee:
The strategic pricing adjustments, implemented on January 1st across our enterprise software suite, resulting in an average price increase of 4%, contributed approximately $250 million to the YoY revenue growth. The larger portion of our revenue beat, however, came from increased volume, driven primarily by the accelerating adoption of our cloud-based solutions and strong performance in our cybersecurity segment.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to the foundry partnerships and how these are being integrated into your product roadmap?

Emily Rodriguez:
Certainly. Our foundry partnerships are integral to our product roadmap. We are actively collaborating with our foundry partners to develop and integrate advanced process technologies into our next-generation products. This includes optimizing our designs for specific process nodes, leveraging advanced packaging solutions, and co-developing new materials and manufacturing techniques. The rollout of these features is being closely coordinated with our product teams to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance. For example, our use of advanced packaging solutions from GlobalFoundries is enabling us to create more compact and powerful chips for our high-performance computing applications.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on inventory management, is this level of efficiency sustainable, or were there one-time gains this quarter?

David Chen:
We believe that the improvements we've made in inventory management are sustainable. While there may have been some one-time gains from specific initiatives, the majority of our progress is due to fundamental improvements in our demand forecasting, supply chain optimization, and production processes. We are committed to maintaining our focus on inventory efficiency and will continue to invest in the tools and processes necessary to achieve our goals. We are targeting a DOI of 65 days by the end of the year, which would represent a significant achievement in our ongoing efforts to optimize working capital and improve profitability.

Closing

Michael Carter:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
